name: Vox
description: Vox combo organ listing copy, scoped to the Jaguar and Continental models (single- and dual-manual) per the Combo Organ Service page listing these as the Vox models CEPCo specializes in. Historical/technical details sourced from Wikipedia and cross-referenced combo organ references; anything not confidently verifiable was left out rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Vox Continental
nodes.copy:
Every Vox combo organ we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and tone. The result is an organ that plays and sounds better than it likely has in decades.

This is Vox's original single-manual Continental, produced between 1962 and 1971 and one of the most recognizable combo organs ever built — instantly identifiable by its reverse-colored keys, orange top, and chrome Z-shaped leg stand. Rather than the rocker-tab voicing found on most combo organs, the Continental uses six slider-style drawbars: two for voice (flute and reed) and four for footage (16', 8', 4', and a mixture drawbar labeled "IV"). Like most combo organs of its era it runs on germanium transistors, which can drift out of tune over time — part of what we address in every restoration. It's the organ behind the Beatles' "Think for Yourself," the Animals' "House of the Rising Sun," the Doors' early recordings including "Light My Fire," and ? and the Mysterians' "96 Tears," and it saw a second life in the late-70s new wave scene with Elvis Costello & the Attractions and Madness.

Features:
- Cleaned, Lubricated & Restored Key Contacts and Bus Bars
- Addressed Germanium Transistor Drift for Stable, In-Tune Voicing
- New Electrolytic Capacitors
- Fully Restored Power Supply
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup
- Cleaned All Drawbars, Switches & Connectors
- All Voltages Checked & Calibrated for Optimum Performance
- New Cables

Included:
- Z-Style Leg Stand

nodes.label: Vox Continental II / Super Continental
nodes.copy:
Every Vox combo organ we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and tone. The result is an organ that plays and sounds better than it likely has in decades.

This is Vox's dual-manual Continental — badged the Continental II in England and the Super Continental in Italy — introduced in 1965. It carries over the single-manual Continental's six-drawbar voicing and adds a 5-1/3' drawbar on the upper manual, an octave of bass keys, and a dedicated string bass feature; later units also add a Hammond-style percussion option.

nodes.label: Vox Jaguar
nodes.copy:
Every Vox combo organ we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and tone. The result is an organ that plays and sounds better than it likely has in decades.

Introduced in 1966 as a budget alternative to the Continental, the Jaguar trades the Continental's drawbars for simple rocker tabs — Flute, Bright, Brass, and Mellow — plus a Bass Chords option and the same vibrato circuit as its bigger sibling. It's a simpler-sounding organ than the Continental (it only generates fundamental frequencies, without the Continental's additional harmonics), but at around 30 lbs it's dramatically easier to haul to a gig. Built in Italy by GEM off a design derived from the Howard combo organ, the Jaguar was also sold in DIY kit form to keep costs down.
